Price momentum corroborates the fair-value anchor: NVDA has returned +21.6% over the trailing 12 months and sits at 81% of its 52-week range with a drawdown of only -6.1% from the 52-week high, so trend persistence is an independent upside driver toward the $231.38 DCF mid.

Balance-sheet capacity underwrites the forecast: stockholders' equity of $228.98B against $91.29B of liabilities (71.5% of $320.27B of assets equity-funded) alongside TTM net income of $192.88B gives the model's 40.0% FY1 revenue growth rate and 30.5%-of-revenue reinvestment program an internally funded base, with no equity issuance assumed in the equity bridge.

Disclosure cadence provides identifiable re-rating checkpoints: 10 SEC 8-K filings were indexed between 2026-03-06 and 2026-09-03, including the 2026-08-17 report of a material agreement (Item 1.01) and a material financial obligation (Item 2.03) and the 2026-09-03 'other events' filing — primary-source disclosure against a $231.38 DCF anchor is the mechanism by which the +1.3% gap to fair value can widen in the holder's favour.
thesis.company_overview:
NVIDIA Corporation designs and sells accelerated-computing platforms — data-center GPU accelerators and integrated systems, networking silicon and software, and the CUDA programming stack — positioning it upstream in the AI supply chain as a merchant supplier of compute to hyperscale, cloud, enterprise and sovereign buyers. The latest 10-K (filed 2026-02-25) lists subsidiaries including Mellanox Technologies, Ltd. (Israel), NVIDIA International, Inc. (Delaware) and NVIDIA Singapore Pte Ltd, consistent with an integrated hardware-plus-networking-plus-software model rather than a single-component vendor. A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Geographic revenue breakdown was likewise not available from the injected SEC XBRL facts and is not cited here.

Scale and profitability are the evidence of the moat. TTM revenue of $302.97B converts to TTM net income of $192.88B, a 63.7% TTM net margin; FY2026 (period ended 2026-01-25) gross profit of $153.46B on revenue of $215.94B is a 71.1% gross margin, with operating income of $130.39B equal to a 60.4% operating margin. Margins at that level in a capital-intensive semiconductor business reflect software/ecosystem lock-in and pricing power rather than commodity silicon economics. The balance sheet reinforces it: $228.98B of stockholders' equity against $91.29B of liabilities on $320.27B of assets, i.e. 71.5% equity-funded, giving the firm the internal capacity to fund a heavy reinvestment program without dilution. The durable moat rests on the CUDA software ecosystem and installed-base switching costs, full-stack integration of compute, networking and systems, and the scale advantage that lets the company out-invest rivals across both silicon and software generations.
thesis.competitor_analysis: No peer comp set was produced for this run — the peer-screen / peer-financials fetch returned no usable data for NVDA — so relative multiple positioning cannot be asserted and no premium or discount to peers is claimed here; any peer-multiple comparison would be fabrication. What can be compared is business-model economics rather than share: an issuer generating TTM revenue of $302.97B at a 71.1% FY2026 gross margin and a 60.4% FY2026 operating margin operates with differentiated IP and ecosystem lock-in economics, not the commodity cost-plus profile of merchant foundry or memory suppliers, and that distinction is the correct axis for peer segmentation (direct accelerator peers, adjacent compute/IP peers, analog/industrial peers and platform leaders are not interchangeable). The absence of a comp set means the valuation conclusion rests on the DCF evidence — a $231.38 mid and a $185.10–$277.66 own range — plus the $228.52 market price, not on relative-multiple triangulation. Until a peer screen is sourced, competitive conclusions are structural (scale, switching costs, integration) rather than multiple-based, and the target carries no peer-relative premium.
key_takeaways: Fair value and spot are coincident: the DCF mid of $231.38 sits just 1.3% above the $228.52 market price, and the method's own band ($185.10–$277.66) brackets the quote — NVDA is priced, not mispriced, which is the core reason for a Hold rather than a Buy.

The earnings base is high-quality: TTM revenue of $302.97B converts to $192.88B of TTM net income (a 63.7% TTM net margin), while FY2026 gross profit of $153.46B on $215.94B of revenue is a 71.1% gross margin and FY2026 operating income of $130.39B a 60.4% operating margin — margin structure of that caliber argues against a Sell even at a full multiple.

The market is not extrapolating an unreachable path: with the model's 10.68% WACC held fixed the reverse-DCF solves to 21.49% flat annual growth over a 10-year horizon, essentially the model's own 21.5% average fade from 40.0% (FY1) to 3.0% (FY10) — and the fade schedule front-loads cash flow, making it the more conservative construct.

Momentum is constructive but leaves thin cushion: +21.6% over the trailing 12 months, an 81% position in the 52-week range and only a -6.1% drawdown from the high mean the stock is already near the upper end of its own range.

Method concentration is the swing factor: a single DCF at data-quality weight 0.85 with no cross-validation widened the published band to $173.53–$289.22, and the $185.10 low end is -19.0% below the current price — the bear case is a re-rating to the low end of the model's own distribution, not a fundamental break.
thesis.narrative:
NVDA is a Hold with a $231.38 target against a $228.52 market price, or +1.3% implied upside. The DCF is the only method that ran this cycle (mid $231.38, own band $185.10–$277.66, data-quality weight 0.85); the peer screen produced no usable comp set and no DDM was computed, so there is no second method to blend and the synthesis carries explicit single-method degradation, widening the published band to $173.53–$289.22 at medium confidence. With fair value and spot within 1.3% of each other, the risk/reward is balanced rather than directional — the stock is priced, not mispriced.

The business earns its multiple. TTM revenue of $302.97B converts to $192.88B of TTM net income, a 63.7% TTM net margin, while FY2026 (period ended 2026-01-25) gross profit of $153.46B on $215.94B of revenue is a 71.1% gross margin and FY2026 operating income of $130.39B a 60.4% operating margin. That profitability is carried on a $228.98B equity base against $91.29B of liabilities — 71.5% of $320.27B of assets equity-funded — which is what allows the model to fund 40.0% FY1 revenue growth fading to 3.0% by FY10 without an equity raise.

The market is not paying for an unreachable path. Holding the 10.68% WACC fixed, the reverse-DCF solves to 21.49% flat annual growth across the 10-year horizon, effectively identical to the model's own 21.5% average fade from 40.0% to 3.0% — and because a front-loaded fade generates more cash early than a flat rate, the model schedule is the more conservative construct. Momentum is supportive but not stretched: +21.6% over the trailing year, an 81% position in the 52-week range, and a -6.1% drawdown from the high. On that evidence the +1.3% gap to $231.38 justifies Hold, with the $185.10 DCF low (-19.0% from spot) as the downside marker and the $277.66 high (+21.5%) as the bull marker.

thesis.tagline: NVDA: DCF fair value $231 vs $228 spot — Hold, +1.3%
thesis.valuation_overview: Only one method was computed this run: a 10-year DCF whose mid case of $231.38 (own band $185.10–$277.66) is built on a WACC of 10.68%, a revenue-growth fade of 40.0% in FY1 to 3.0% in FY10 (21.5% average) and a 3.0% perpetuity growth rate applied after the explicit window. That mid lands 1.3% above the $228.52 market price. No comps or DDM were produced — the peer screen returned no usable comp set — so there is no second method to blend, the weighted target equals the DCF mid, and the synthesis flagged single-method degradation, widening the published band to $173.53–$289.22 (±25%) at medium confidence. The divergence between methods that would normally explain a wide band is therefore unavailable as evidence; confidence rests on the internal coherence of the DCF. Cross-checking via reverse-DCF, the market price solves to a 10.74% implied WACC when the growth fade is held fixed (versus the model's 10.68%), and to 21.49% flat annual growth when WACC is held fixed — against the model's own 21.5% average fade. Because the fade schedule and the market-implied flat rate average ~21.5%, price and modelled fair value are effectively coincident, which is precisely why the verdict is Hold rather than Buy.
